selectedLines: The 2026 election guide contains 495 sourced candidate records across 15 affiliations: 408 Assembly and 87 Council. A scoped update on 1 November 2026 added 13 primary-sourced announcements and flagged two reported status discrepancies. Other records retain their own check dates; this was not a full-field review. Candidate names, status and source links come first; coverage and provenance remain inspectable. Announcements and preselections are distinct from accepted VEC nominations. The directory is not a complete ballot.
The workbench does not submit nominations, collect payments or private nominator details. Corrections should retain the source, checked date and reason for change. Repository and project maintenance.

Begin with the relevant community-controlled organisation’s published priorities and invitation to participate. Ask government which decision, budget and outcome changed under each Priority Reform. Initial submissions to the 2026 review were due on 26 October 2026. The Productivity Commission is preparing a draft report, with a “What we heard” paper planned for February 2027 and a draft report for April 2027. Follow the review page for the next opportunity to comment. This timetable was checked on 2 November 2026. Communities choose what information they share.

DCCEEW’s 30 October 2026 update reports that around three-quarters of Australian gas production is exported. Legislation for the reservation scheme has been introduced to Parliament. The department describes commencement in early 2027, with the principal legislation and licensing framework to commence by proclamation no later than 1 July 2027; supply obligations are planned from 1 January 2028. The proposed domestic supply obligation is up to 20% of annual LNG export volumes, with adjustment mechanisms. Exposure-draft consultation closed on 24 September 2026; current rules remain until new arrangements are implemented. This status was checked on 2 November 2026.
